open_obligations: Check whether the DPO training runs show any of the honest-then-lying cycling Irving et al. describe, or whether too few iterations were run to observe it.
Confirm that judge accuracy, not only debater win rate, was tracked across all checkpoints.
Note the judge is never trained on the debaters' transcripts, and check how it compares with the judge in Irving et al.'s proposal.
out.other_title: Does self-play training stably converge to honest debate equilibria?
out.rationale: Irving et al. ask whether self-play stably converges to honest debate equilibria and know of no theory guaranteeing it. Arnesen et al. report that self-play DPO training of their debaters is associated with 4 percentage points higher judge accuracy for the fully DPO-trained model than for the SFT model (p < 10^-6); this is empirical evidence comparing the fully DPO-trained and SFT debaters with a judge never trained on their transcripts, not a convergence result.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether self-play training of debaters moves toward truth-favouring outcomes rather than unstable cycles, for DPO-trained debater models

open_obligations: Check whether the trained dishonest debater became more deceptive, which would bear on equilibrium safety.
Check whether the Llama3-8B debaters started from an RLHF-tuned model.
Check that the 4-point gain holds across question subsets.
out.other_title: Inference-only debate with RLHF-honest models says little about debate as training
out.rationale: Kenton et al. say inference-only prompting gives little evidence about equilibria reached by training. Arnesen et al. train debaters with DPO and report the fully trained debater is associated with 4 percentage points higher judge accuracy than the SFT model (p < 10^-6), while consultant skill shows no apparent relationship with judge accuracy.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether conclusions from inference-only debate carry over when debaters are trained, on QuALITY-HARD

open_obligations: Check whether the dishonest debater's strategies changed qualitatively during training.
Note the judge is an LLM, not a human.
Check whether stronger base models would find strategies that reduce accuracy.
Check how far the trained Llama3-8B debaters are from equilibrium.

Note that Michael et al.'s debaters were humans, whereas Arnesen et al.'s are DPO-trained models, and check whether that training puts more optimisation pressure on debaters than Michael et al.'s human debaters faced.
out.other_title: Undiscovered dishonest strategies could break debate at Nash equilibrium
out.rationale: Michael et al. say addressing whether debate works in the limit needs more optimisation pressure on debaters. Arnesen et al. train debaters with self-play DPO and report +4 points judge accuracy versus the SFT model.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether training debaters to win keeps judge accuracy rising, for self-play DPO Llama3-8B debaters on QuALITY-HARD

open_obligations: Check whether the fine-tuned GPT-4-Turbo judge explains the absence of a negative effect.
Note DPO training versus best-of-N and critique-and-refinement optimisation.
Check whether consultant persuasiveness actually increased much under DPO.
out.other_title: More persuasive consultants lower judge accuracy; optimisation favours incorrect side
out.rationale: Khan et al. report that best-of-N and critique-and-refinement make consultants relatively more persuasive for the incorrect answer, lowering judge accuracy. Arnesen et al. find no apparent relationship between trained consultant skill and judge accuracy; Arnesen et al. train Llama3-8B with DPO and use a fine-tuned GPT-4-Turbo judge, while Khan et al. apply best-of-N and critique-and-refinement to consultant models fine-tuned using RLHF, which tend to already perform well when advocating correct answers, and they give this as the reason optimisation might disproportionately improve advocacy for incorrect answers.
out.scope: proposed CHALLENGES: how optimising consultants for persuasiveness affects judge accuracy on QuALITY

open_obligations: Check whether either judge is fine-tuned, and on what data; the passages say only that Arnesen et al.'s judge is never trained on transcripts from these debaters and that Khan et al. use GPT-4-Turbo to judge their debates.
Note training-based versus inference-time debater improvement.
Check that both use the same correct-answer versus best-distractor framing.
out.other_title: Self-play debate: judge accuracy rises with debater aggregate rating
out.rationale: Khan et al., who use GPT-4-Turbo to judge their debates, report a strong correlation between judge accuracy and debater aggregate rating: as debaters are optimised against win rate (judge preference), judge accuracy improves. Arnesen et al. report that the fully DPO-trained debate model is associated with 4 percentage points higher judge accuracy than the SFT model (p < 10^-6), although the judge is never trained on transcripts from these debaters.
out.scope: proposed SUPPORTS: whether stronger debaters yield higher judge accuracy
